name: naval-descent
_note_fa85: FA-85 (Sept 11, 2026): the expedition marshal stages at BORDELAIS, a controlled Atlantic yard OUTSIDE the Descent camp set (Flanders/Artois/Normandy/Brittany). Normandy was never a yard, so both land lines were refused and the archived naval digest carried zero expedition evidence; Brittany (REPRO_J5 pick) is a camp province and would perturb the staging this script measures. The driver flags a run SCRIPT PRECONDITION when every land line is refused.
_note_phase3: FA slice 17 Phase 3 (Sept 11, 2026): staging Soult at the yard was not enough — the transports lift 15,000 and NO boot French corps is under it (Soult 28,940 refused twice, 'cannot be lightened: a garrison detaches a fixed 3,000 and we already hold our 3'; Napoleon's 10,000 Guard may not sail). The script now follows the lift counsel's OWN road (FA-D16, THE_LIFT_COUNSEL_NAMES_THE_MARSHALATE): commission the cheapest bench marshal (Oudinot, 3,500g, a 5,000-man corps at Paris) on turn 3, march him to Bordelais, and put him into the transports for Munster. Measured on the mock parser: the expedition is drawn up at 72 in 100, lands, takes Munster, and the Royal Navy's counter-landing (Moore) retakes it — the whole Free Ireland arc end to end. The camp/diversion half of the Descent (Ney at Flanders, Davout at Normandy, blockade, the Grand Diversion) is kept exactly as before.

5: land Oudinot in Munster with 5,000 men

_note_sfv6: SF-V6 (Score Finish Step 6, October 4, 2026): since SR-5a trimmed France's boot Net to 1,032 the loop-3 commission behind three keels was refused for gold (1,868g against 3,500g), so the arm never quoted a landing and every later Oudinot line named a man who did not exist. Re-staged on the game's own terms: no gold spent before the commission (loop 4, ~3,880g in the chest); Oudinot marches the loop he is raised to NORMANDY — a French dockyard since NUI-2 moved it from Flanders, with Davout's corps beside it — and sails on loop 5 at full strength, before a British descent can find him on the road (measured: staged at Bordelais on loop 10 he was caught twice by Paget in Guyenne and landed 3,457 men, a raiding party that holds no homeland, VP-R1 b). The expedition is drawn up at 75 in 100, lands 5,000 men and takes Munster (the capture question). The keels come after (loops 6, 7, 9).
